query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A data‐driven inverse design approach using machine learning–assisted surrogate modeling can guide the rapid discovery of intrinsically strong, ductile, and low–weight refractory HEA compositions by efficiently navigating the vast compositional space and predicting optimal multi‐objective properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-principal element refractory HEA systems with a broad, largely unexplored compositional landscape.
generation.intervention: Implement a workflow that integrates high-throughput computational screening with machine learning surrogate models and multi-objective optimization to predict candidate compositions.
generation.conditions: Simulated ambient and high-temperature environments under which the mechanical properties such as strength and ductility are critical, as well as scenarios necessitating low density.
generation.structural_mediator: The predicted phase stability and microstructural homogeneity (e.g., uniform crystal lattice and minimal secondary phase formation) as inferred from the computational descriptors.
generation.mechanism: The machine learning models correlate alloy composition parameters and fast-to-compute physical descriptors (e.g., mixing enthalpy, atomic size mismatch) with key mechanical properties. Through iterative optimization, the approach identifies compositions where these mediators yield improved strength, ductility, and reduced weight compared to conventional designs.
generation.predicted_outcome: Discovery of refractory HEA compositions with a balanced combination of high strength, enhanced ductility, and lower weight, outperforming alloys designed solely by traditional thermo-kinetic simulations.
generation.baseline: Traditional alloy design approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and brute-force computational simulations that are slower for exploring large compositional spaces.
generation.boundary: The surrogate models’ accuracy is confined to the range of composition and property data available during training; predictions may become less reliable for compositions outside this range or under untested conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The success of the inverse design approach relies on the availability and quality of training data. Uncertainties remain regarding the precise magnitude of property improvements and the potential gap between computational predictions and experimental realizations.

falsification_experiment.design: Collect an extensive dataset of refractory HEA compositions and their experimentally measured mechanical properties. Train machine learning surrogate models using part of the dataset. Use the inverse design workflow to predict a set of optimal alloy compositions. Synthesize these predicted alloys and conduct experiments to measure their strength, ductility, and weight to verify if they meet or exceed performance targets relative to traditional designs.
measurements: phase homogeneity (e.g., via XRD and microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the newly synthesized alloys do not exhibit significant improvements in the targeted mechanical properties (i.e., they do not achieve a superior combination of strength, ductility, and low weight compared to alloys designed by conventional methods) or if the predicted mediators (phase stability and homogeneity) do not correlate with the observed properties, the hypothesis will be falsified.
